title: Canary Rollout of a New Model Version
intro: A new model can look better offline and still be worse in production. Canary rollouts let real traffic decide — safely — exactly like a canary code deploy.

steps.prompt: Update fraud-model to the v8 artifact, sending only 10% of traffic to it.
steps.explanation: v7 keeps 90% of traffic; v8 gets 10%.
steps.why: A model with better offline metrics can still fail in production — different data, latency, edge cases. Limiting exposure to 10% caps the damage while you gather evidence.

steps.prompt: Confirm the traffic split is in effect.
steps.fake_output:
NAME          READY  PREV  LATEST  URL
fraud-model   True   90    10      http://fraud-model.ml.example.com
steps.why: Verify the split before trusting any comparison — a misapplied patch that sent 100% or 0% to v8 invalidates everything you conclude next.

steps.prompt: Compare latency between the two revisions.
steps.why: Compare the SAME metric split by revision, over the same window — the canary is only meaningful as a relative comparison, not against a fixed number.

steps.prompt: Compare the positive-prediction rate between revisions — a big divergence would be a red flag.
steps.explanation: Similar rates — v8 isn't behaving wildly differently.
steps.why: For models, 'no errors' isn't enough: the distribution of outputs must also be sane. Once ground-truth labels arrive (e.g. confirmed fraud), compare precision/recall per revision too.

steps.prompt: Metrics look healthy. Promote v8 to 100% of traffic.
steps.explanation: v8 now serves all traffic; v7 remains available as a rollback target.
steps.why: Rolling back is just setting canaryTrafficPercent back to 0 — the model-serving equivalent of the blue-green selector switch in cicd-tutorial-009.
